previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a homeless man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and alcohol use disorder, was admitted for chest pain and alcohol intoxication. He exhibited mild alcohol withdrawal symptoms, which resolved with minimal benzodiazepine use and supportive care. His chest pain was determined to be non-cardiac, likely due to cervical spine degenerative changes affecting nerve roots, and was managed with gabapentin and a lidocaine patch. A CT scan incidentally revealed right lower lobe pneumonia, which was improving clinically and radiologically, requiring no further antibiotics. His chronic conditions, including pulmonary embolism, were stabilized with continued enoxaparin, heart failure medications, and B12 supplementation. He remained compliant with anticoagulation and was discharged home to a shelter with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider and psychiatry for ongoing management of substance use, depression, and cardiac health.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M homeless man with alcohol abuse, Pulmonary embolism (PE) 
on lovenox injections, atrial fibrillation, systolic CHF with EF 
25% s/p pacemaker placement presenting with chest pain, alcohol 
intoxication, and hypoxia.
. 
# HYPOXIA: 
He received 3L of IV fluids in the ED for aggressive 
resuscitation of elevated lactate. He became dyspneic and 
hypoxic on arrival the floor, thought to be related to his CHF 
with 25% LVEF. Concern was also for a possible PE, but he 
assured us of his lovenox compliance so heart failure was felt 
to be more likely. He was aggressively diuresed and returned to 
room air within days. He was then restarted on his home lasix 
dose.
.
#ETOH ABUSE: 
Found to have a positive EtOH in the ED. He was started on CIWA 
scale with valium PRN. He initially required a couple doses 
daily of valium, but this was quickly tapered. He did not 
require additional valium on the last 2 days of his hospital 
stay. He was given thiamine, folate and MVI. Social work was 
called to assist with resources for outpatient detox.
.
#CHEST PAIN:
Patient with left subcostal pain of unclear etiology. This 
appears to be a chronic complaint. Unlikely to be cardaic given 
normal biomarkers and ECG. Recurrence of PE was thought to be 
possible, but a repeat CTA showed that the PE had actually 
improved. A RUQ U/S was also performed, which was unremarkable. 
Pain appeared somewhat improved on discharge. Would consider 
lidocaine patch if pain continues.
.  
# PULMONARY EMBOLISM:
Recently diagnosed PE ___ and has been on lovenox. There was 
a question of his compliance, but he assured us that he had the 
medication and was taking it regularly. Repeat CTA showed that 
the PE had improved. Continue lovenox ___ daily.
.  
#ATRIAL FIBRILLATION: History of atrial fibrillation although 
currently in sinus rhythm. Previously on dabigatran. CHADS2 
score of 2 (HTN, CHF), currently on lovenox for pulmonary 
embolism. Continued metoprolol
.  
# HTN: Controlled with home medications, some of the 
hypertension on admission is also secondary to alcohol withdrawl

# HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA:

3.0 during admission. RUQ ultrasound was unremarkable. T Bili 
improved on discharge. Would continue to trend as needed as an 
outpatient.
.
# HEMOPTYSIS: Mildly pink sputum, frothy on examination, 
consistent with heart failure and volume overload. 
.

arrival to the floor hypoxic, tachypnic, with rales midway up
